reason: Selected replication and prompt ablations motivate stress-testing context arbitration across model families.

candidates.title: Stress-test conflicting evidence under prompt variants
candidates.rule: When relying on supplied facts that conflict with a model’s prior knowledge, test multiple question phrasings and context layouts for each target model rather than assuming a stable tendency to trust context.
candidates.passage: question phrasing, filler content, and conflict position can swing the outcome by tens of percentage points.
candidates.finding: Across thirty-one open models, post-training effects change direction by family, and irrelevant filler can increase or decrease reliance on contextual answers. The recommendation is inferred from behavioral sensitivity, not a tested conflict-resolution policy.
candidates.conditions: Tests compare memorized and supplied contradictory answers; access to prediction probabilities limits the model panel.
candidates.limitations: Following context is not automatically correct: supplied facts can be false. The paper’s abstract and body report different maximum phrasing swings; avoid presenting either as a universal magnitude. No temporal knowledge-update or production RAG guarantee follows.
candidates.validation_test: Evaluate true corrections and false distractors under varied templates, source positions and fillers; measure correctness and justified abstention separately from mere context obedience.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
